recipes.name: Cornbread
recipes.description: Golden, tender cornbread with a crisp edge.

less.note: Traditional cornbread uses little sugar, so you can halve it without changing the texture - it simply tastes more savory.

profileOverrides.prep: Grease your pan ({pan}) well. For a crisper crust, put the greased pan in the oven while it preheats.
profileOverrides.cook: Pour the batter into the pan. Bake at {temp} for {time}, until golden and the edges pull away from the pan.
profileOverrides.check: A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean.
notes: A hot, greased pan gives cornbread a crisp bottom and edge.
Cornbread dries out if overbaked - check at the early end of the range.

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, cornmeal, baking powder, salt and sugar.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the milk, oil and egg until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the cornbread cool in the pan for 10 minutes before cutting.

tips: Use fresh baking powder - old powder makes dense cornbread.
A cast-iron skillet gives the best crust.
Let the batter stand 5 minutes so the cornmeal can absorb some moisture.

panOptions.text: 8×8 in / 20×20 cm square pan or 8 in / 20 cm cast-iron skillet

recipes.name: Irish Soda Bread
recipes.description: A rustic, no-yeast loaf with a crisp crust and tender crumb.

less.note: Soda bread uses only a tablespoon of sugar, so halving it makes very little difference.

profileOverrides.prep: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or dust a cast-iron skillet with flour.
profileOverrides.cook: Bake the loaf at {temp} for {time}, until deep golden brown.
profileOverrides.check: The loaf should sound hollow when you tap the bottom.
notes: Work quickly - the baking soda starts reacting as soon as it meets the buttermilk.
Wrap the cooled loaf in a clean towel to keep the crust soft.

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt and sugar.

steps.title: Cut In the Butter
steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture looks like fine crumbs.

steps.title: Add the Buttermilk
steps.text: Pour in the buttermilk and stir with a fork until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overwork it.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Turn the dough onto a floured surface, knead just 5-6 times and shape into a round about 4 cm (1 1/2 in) thick. Place it on your sheet ({pan}) and cut a deep cross about 2 cm (3/4 in) into the top.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on a wire rack for at least 20 minutes before slicing.

tips: Use real buttermilk (or milk with a splash of lemon juice) - the acid activates the baking soda.
Do not knead for long; soda bread is best handled very little.
Cut the cross deep so the center bakes through.

panOptions.text: one round loaf on a baking sheet
two or three round loaves on baking sheets (about 2 cups of flour each)
